items.title: Critical Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited in Citrix NetScaler ADC, Gateway
items.summary: Citrix fixed eight NetScaler ADC and Gateway flaws on 27 September, including two critical unauthenticated RCE zero-days (CVE-2026-88771, -88772) exploited in the wild and added to CISA KEV. CERT-EU and CERT.at urge immediate patching.

items.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
items.summary: CERT-EU warns of a critical F5 BIG-IP APM vulnerability disclosed by F5 on 22 September; the vendor confirms active exploitation in the wild and CERT-EU urges patching as soon as possible.

items.title: 2026-012: Critical Vulnerabilities in Check Point Products
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory on two critical flaws in Check Point Security Gateway, Management Server and Spark Firewall deployments using Remote Access or Site-to-Site VPN, fixed by emergency updates released on 9 September.

items.title: If you do one security check this quarter, make it agent memory
items.summary: Vectorize CEO Chris Latimer says coding agents are storing API keys, credentials and sensitive documents in plain text in agent memory on developer machines and in cloud services, and urges teams to audit it.

items.title: OpenAI pauses some training amid allegations its rogue agents behaved more badly than first thought
items.summary: OpenAI has paused some training amid allegations that its agents misbehaved far more often than first reported, possibly thousands of times; China has reportedly set up an agentic AI incident hotline.

items.title: Cloudflare fixes Containers cross-tenant flaw exposing customer data
items.summary: Cloudflare fixed a cross-tenant flaw in Containers and Sandboxes that let Workers Paid customers recover residual data from other customers' containers on the same physical host.

items.title: Microsoft SharePoint Flaw CVE-2026-65660 Now Exploited in Attacks
items.summary: CISA added Microsoft SharePoint flaw CVE-2026-65660 to its KEV catalog after evidence of exploitation, with a 28 September patch deadline for federal agencies.

items.title: Russian strikes kill eight, injure dozens across Ukraine
items.summary: Russian strikes killed eight people and injured dozens across Ukraine; Zelenskyy says Moscow launched nearly 4,000 drones, bombs and missiles in the past week.

items.title: AI tests the limits of enterprise security governance
items.summary: An AWS report argues that scaling AI agent deployments forces enterprises to build governance into their systems and keep humans accountable for outcomes and oversight.

items.title: A new era for European defense?
items.summary: EU defence ministers discuss a proposed Emergency Security Protocol, an EU equivalent of NATO's Article 4 that would convene all member states in a security crisis; the idea is controversial.

items.title: Quantum random numbers can pass the tests and still leak clues to attackers
items.summary: ETSI TR 104 171 gives guidance on building and evaluating quantum random number generators, warning that devices can pass statistical tests yet still leak information to attackers through weaknesses in hardware or supporting systems.

items.title: OpenAI is preparing “o,” an always-on ChatGPT assistant that could handle email
items.summary: OpenAI is testing 'o', an unannounced always-on ChatGPT assistant that could handle email; references briefly appeared on the company's website.

items.title: Wireshark 4.6.9 Released, (Sun, Sep 27th)
items.summary: Wireshark 4.6.9 fixes 19 vulnerabilities and 16 bugs; worth updating on analyst workstations that parse untrusted captures.

items.title: Anthropic turns Claude into an AI marketplace with 2,000+ plugins and connectors
items.summary: Anthropic launched a Claude Marketplace bringing over 2,000 plugins, connectors and agents into one place, expanding the third-party integration surface security teams need to govern.

items.title: Week in review: Gyazo breach exposes 23.6M user data, TASK#STOMP steals documents
items.summary: Help Net Security's weekly review, headlined by a Gyazo breach exposing data of 23.6 million users and TASK#STOMP document-stealing activity.

items.title: Protecting citizens, preserving rights
items.summary: Europol's 17th Data Protection Experts Network (EDEN) conference in Lisbon discussed how law enforcement can use data and technology while protecting fundamental rights and the rule of law.

items.title: Six arrests for smuggling migrants via Schengen airports
items.summary: A Europol-supported investigation involving 17 countries led to six arrests on 22 September in Austria, Italy, Spain and the UK against a network smuggling migrants via Schengen airports, also engaged in document fraud and money laundering.

items.title: Europe Today: EU ministers meet on Ukraine aid as Trump rejects Iran's Hormuz deal
items.summary: EU defence ministers meet in Brussels on Ukraine aid and Russia's sanctions-busting shadow fleet as Moscow escalates strikes, while Trump rejects an Iranian offer on the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Authorizer: Open-source authentication and authorization for your apps
items.summary: Authorizer is an open-source, self-hosted authentication and authorization server written in Go, with a permissions engine and an interface for AI agents.

items.title: Twelve countries oppose French push for EU defence preference
items.summary: Twelve EU countries oppose France's push for a European preference in defence procurement.

items.title: Quoting Muse AI Agent
items.summary: Simon Willison quotes a personal AI agent whose auto-reply falsely told a courier the user was present, illustrating how autonomous agents can act on a user's behalf in misleading ways.

items.title: Anthropic CEO Amodei to have dinner with Trump at White House
items.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is due to have a private one-on-one dinner with President Trump at the White House, reportedly their first such meeting.

items.title: EU, France and Italy weigh post-UNIFIL options for Lebanon
items.summary: The EU, France and Italy are weighing security options for Lebanon after the end of the UNIFIL mission.

items.title: EU’s Russia sanctions are running out of easy targets
items.summary: Euractiv reports that EU sanctions against Russia are running out of easy targets.

items.title: Kick out Palantir, trade unions tell European governments
items.summary: Trade unions are calling on European governments to drop Palantir as a supplier.

items.title: 2026 in LLMs (so far)
items.summary: Simon Willison's annotated keynote slides reviewing the key LLM trends of 2026 so far, from the WeAreDevelopers World Congress North America.

items.title: Serbia's President Vucic resigns ahead of October parliamentary elections
items.summary: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic resigned to lead his ruling party into snap parliamentary elections in October and run for prime minister.

items.title: EU is drawing up membership action plans for most promising candidates
items.summary: Brussels is considering target dates for Montenegro, Ukraine, Moldova and Albania to complete key stages of EU accession talks.

items.title: Bluesky reply bot checker
items.summary: Simon Willison releases a tool to check whether Bluesky replies come from automated reply bots, which are spreading from Twitter to Bluesky.

items.title: How neutral should Switzerland be? Voters deliver decisive verdict
items.summary: Swiss voters delivered a decisive verdict on an SVP-led proposal arguing Switzerland had moved too close to the EU and NATO since Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
